authority.whyGame: Do not trust the client's number.

expansions.title: Authority as a door
expansions.detail: If authority is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Authority as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for authority live on a row. Health clamped between zero and MaxHealth, then a branch that logs death at zero reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Authority as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for Any Damage. They do not subtracting with no clamp so health goes negative and the death branch never sees zero.

quiz.prompt: Who writes replicated health?
choices: The machine with authority. A client can ask, and must not apply the number itself.
Every client, so the hit marker appears before the server is bothered.
The widget, by editing the text of the health bar.
OnRep, which subtracts again when the value arrives.
quiz.why: Authority writes. Clients ask.
quiz.review_prompt: Who writes replicated health?

quiz.prompt: A client subtracts health locally and also sends the new value to the server. What can the server do?
choices: Reject it. The server decides the damage. The client's number is a request at most.
Accept it, because the client saw the hit first.
Average it with the other clients' guesses.
Ignore combat until the next map load.
quiz.why: Do not trust the client's number.
quiz.review_prompt: A client subtracts health locally and also sends the new value to the server. What can the server do?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The machine with authority writes shared gameplay state. A client can ask.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The machine with authority writes shared gameplay state. A client can ask.

quiz.prompt: True or false: A client may write replicated health so the shooter sees the result a frame sooner, and the server will adopt that write.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The server does not adopt the client's write.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A client may write replicated health so the shooter sees the result a frame sooner, and the server will adopt that write.

quiz.prompt: Where does the damage calculation belong?
choices: On the authority, inside the damage path that owns health.
On each client, inside Tick, using that client's clock.
In the HUD paint function.
In the projectile's cosmetic trail.
quiz.why: The owner of the variable does the math.
quiz.review_prompt: Where does the damage calculation belong?

quiz.prompt: Two players shoot the same target in one frame. Who produces the one health value everyone else will see?
choices: The authority, applying both hits in its order.
Whichever client has the lower ping.
Both clients, and replication unions the two floats.
The target's OnRep, which picks the prettier number.
quiz.why: One writer.
quiz.review_prompt: Two players shoot the same target in one frame. Who produces the one health value everyone else will see?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A server RPC is a way for the client to ask. The function that runs on the server is what decides.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Ask, then decide.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A server RPC is a way for the client to ask. The function that runs on the server is what decides.

quiz.prompt: Health is correct on the server and wrong on a proxy. What did the proxy likely do?
choices: It applied damage locally instead of waiting for the replicated value.
It rendered too many polygons.
It used the wrong input action for movement.
It forgot to cast to the door Blueprint.
quiz.why: Proxies display. They do not decide.
quiz.review_prompt: Health is correct on the server and wrong on a proxy. What did the proxy likely do?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Making the variable replicated is enough. Any machine may still be the one that assigns it.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Replication copies the authority's value. It does not elect a writer.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Making the variable replicated is enough. Any machine may still be the one that assigns it.

quiz.prompt: A listen-server host is also a player. Whose health write still counts?
choices: The authority write, including when the host is the player who got hit.
The remote client's write, because the host is 'just another player'.
The UI on the host, which is closer to the screen.
No write. Listen servers skip replication.
quiz.why: The host's authority is still the authority.
quiz.review_prompt: A listen-server host is also a player. Whose health write still counts?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Playing the hit flash on the client requires the client to also subtract health, or the flash has no number to show.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The flash reads the replicated number.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Playing the hit flash on the client requires the client to also subtract health, or the flash has no number to show.

quiz.prompt: What does the player on a remote machine see if the client subtracted and the server did not?
choices: A health bar that snaps back when the real value arrives, or a kill the server never agreed to.
A smoother game, with no later correction.
The server crashes, because clients are not allowed to send packets.
Fog of war clears.
quiz.why: Prediction without authority pops.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the player on a remote machine see if the client subtracted and the server did not?

property.whyGame: Replicate the number that selects the reaction.

expansions.title: Replicated properties as a door
expansions.detail: If replicated properties is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Replicated properties as data

quiz.prompt: What should replicate for a health bar?
choices: The health property. Not the mesh, and not the widget.
The skeletal mesh, so every bone pose is the health.
The widget object itself.
The player's mouse position.
quiz.why: Replicate the number.
quiz.review_prompt: What should replicate for a health bar?

quiz.prompt: A designer replicates the actor's mesh pointer so other machines build the wounded model. What is expensive and unnecessary?
choices: Sending the mesh when a single float would tell the other machines which pose to play.
Sending the float, which is larger than a mesh.
Not replicating anything, because meshes update themselves.
Replicating the player name.

quiz.review_prompt: A designer replicates the actor's mesh pointer so other machines build the wounded model. What is expensive and unnecessary?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Replicate the number. Do not replicate the mesh or the widget.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Replicate the number. Do not replicate the mesh or the widget.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Widgets should be replicated so every client shares one UMG object.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Widgets are local.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Widgets should be replicated so every client shares one UMG object.

quiz.prompt: Ammo in a magazine should replicate as what?
choices: The integer count. Each client builds the HUD from that count.
The bullet mesh instances, one replicated actor per round.
The reload montage asset pointer.
The input action object.
quiz.why: The count is the property.
quiz.review_prompt: Ammo in a magazine should replicate as what?

quiz.prompt: Who creates the health bar widget?
choices: Each client, locally, when it needs to draw. The widget reads the replicated health.
The server, which replicates the widget pointer to everyone.
The projectile that dealt the damage.
Begin Play on the server only, with clients left blank.
quiz.why: UI is local.
quiz.review_prompt: Who creates the health bar widget?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A replicated float is enough for every client to play its own hit reaction in OnRep.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The number arrives. The reaction is local.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A replicated float is enough for every client to play its own hit reaction in OnRep.

quiz.prompt: Equipped weapon visuals differ per id. What replicates?
choices: The equipped id. Each client looks up the meshes from that id.
Every mesh on the gun, every attachment, and the material instances.
The gunsmith data asset pointer only, with no id.
Nothing. Weapons are not visible to other players.
quiz.why: Replicate the id, not the meshes.
quiz.review_prompt: Equipped weapon visuals differ per id. What replicates?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Replicating the mesh is safer because a float might compress.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The float is the cheap, sufficient fact.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Replicating the mesh is safer because a float might compress.

quiz.prompt: A scoreboard needs the score. What is the replicated property?
choices: The score number. The board widget is created locally and reads it.
The scoreboard widget class, spawned on the server and replicated.
The medal montage.
The mouse cursor.
quiz.why: The number travels. The board does not.
quiz.review_prompt: A scoreboard needs the score. What is the replicated property?

quiz.prompt: True or false: If the mesh is not replicated, other players cannot see the character at all.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The pawn can still replicate movement. The mesh is the local asset.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: If the mesh is not replicated, other players cannot see the character at all.

quiz.prompt: What breaks if the widget is the replicated object and the health float is not?
choices: Clients share a UI object they cannot sensibly share, and they still do not know the health.
Nothing. Widgets replicate more cheaply than floats.
Movement stops.
Input tags all activate.
quiz.why: Replicate the fact the UI displays.
quiz.review_prompt: What breaks if the widget is the replicated object and the health float is not?

onrep.whyGame: Play the hit. Do not decide the rule there.

expansions.title: OnRep as a door
expansions.detail: If onrep is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: OnRep as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for onrep live on a row. Health clamped between zero and MaxHealth, then a branch that logs death at zero reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: OnRep as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for Any Damage. They do not subtracting with no clamp so health goes negative and the death branch never sees zero.

quiz.prompt: When does OnRep run?
choices: When the replicated value arrives on a machine that did not write it.
Every Tick, so the reaction cannot miss a frame.
In the constructor, before the value exists.
When the player presses any input.
quiz.why: OnRep is the arrival.
quiz.review_prompt: When does OnRep run?

quiz.prompt: Health just replicated down. What should OnRep_Health do?
choices: Play the hit reaction and leave the float alone.
Subtract the damage again, so the proxy 'agrees' with the hit.
Write a new health and send it back to the server.
Open the inventory.
quiz.why: Play the hit. Do not decide the rule there.
quiz.review_prompt: Health just replicated down. What should OnRep_Health do?

quiz.prompt: True or false: OnRep is where other machines hear the new value. Play the hit there, do not decide the rule there.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: OnRep is where other machines hear the new value. Play the hit there, do not decide the rule there.

quiz.prompt: True or false: OnRep is a second chance to apply the gameplay rule, in case the authority was wrong.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: OnRep is not a second authority.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: OnRep is a second chance to apply the gameplay rule, in case the authority was wrong.

quiz.prompt: A limp starts in OnRep when a limb value changes. Where was the limp amount decided?
choices: On the authority, before the value replicated.
Inside OnRep, which is the first time anyone does the math.
In the animation blueprint, which writes the replicated float.
On the client that shot, which replicated its own result.
quiz.why: The authority decides. OnRep performs.
quiz.review_prompt: A limp starts in OnRep when a limb value changes. Where was the limp amount decided?

quiz.prompt: OnRep adds 10 to score because the board 'should tick up'. The authority already added 10. What is the score?
choices: 20 on that client, 10 on the authority.
10 everywhere, because OnRep additions are ignored.
0, because double writes cancel.
The widget's font size.
quiz.why: Do not apply the rule twice.
quiz.review_prompt: OnRep adds 10 to score because the board 'should tick up'. The authority already added 10. What is the score?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A cosmetic flash, a sound, or a limp belongs in OnRep. The subtract does not.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Show the change. Do not make it.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A cosmetic flash, a sound, or a limp belongs in OnRep. The subtract does not.

quiz.prompt: The server is the machine that wrote health. Does its OnRep need to subtract?
choices: No. The server already wrote the value. OnRep is for the others, and it still must not subtract.
Yes. Otherwise the server's health is only half applied.
Only if Tick did not run that frame.
Only for the host's HUD font.
quiz.why: The writer does not reapply.
quiz.review_prompt: The server is the machine that wrote health. Does its OnRep need to subtract?

quiz.prompt: True or false: OnRep runs before the property has changed, so you must assign the property inside it.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: OnRep runs because the property changed.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: OnRep runs before the property has changed, so you must assign the property inside it.

quiz.prompt: A door's IsOpen replicates. OnRep plays the swing. What must it not do?
choices: Toggle IsOpen again, which would fight the replicated value.
Read IsOpen.
Play a sound.
Ignore the value and do nothing, which is also wrong if a swing was required, but the bug to avoid is writing.
quiz.why: Read and perform. Do not write.
quiz.review_prompt: A door's IsOpen replicates. OnRep plays the swing. What must it not do?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Skipping OnRep and polling the replicated value from Tick is the same, just more reliable.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Tick polls. OnRep is the edge.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Skipping OnRep and polling the replicated value from Tick is the same, just more reliable.

quiz.prompt: What does a remote player see if OnRep subtracts and the next replication arrives?
choices: A correction. The bar jumps because the local subtract and the server value disagreed.
A perfectly smooth death.
Nothing. Subtracts in OnRep are discarded.
The server adopts the remote subtract.
quiz.why: Corrections are the symptom.
quiz.review_prompt: What does a remote player see if OnRep subtracts and the next replication arrives?

rpc.plainEnglish: Server RPC asks. The server decides.
rpc.whyGame: Do not trust the client's number.

expansions.title: RPCs as a door
expansions.detail: If rpcs is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: RPCs as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for rpcs live on a row. Health clamped between zero and MaxHealth, then a branch that logs death at zero reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: RPCs as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for Any Damage. They do not subtracting with no clamp so health goes negative and the death branch never sees zero.

quiz.prompt: Which RPC should a client use to ask for damage?
choices: A server RPC. The server function decides the number.
A client RPC from the victim to itself.
A multicast that tells every machine to subtract whatever the shooter sent.
No RPC. The client writes health directly.
quiz.why: Server RPC asks. The server decides.
quiz.review_prompt: Which RPC should a client use to ask for damage?

quiz.prompt: The client sends Damage = 99999 in the server RPC. What should the server function do?
choices: Ignore that number and compute the damage itself.
Apply 99999, because the RPC is a trusted message.
Average 99999 with the victim's health.
Forward 99999 to every client in a multicast and let them apply it.
quiz.why: Do not trust the client's number.
quiz.review_prompt: The client sends Damage = 99999 in the server RPC. What should the server function do?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A server RPC asks. The server function decides. Do not trust the client's number.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A server RPC asks. The server function decides. Do not trust the client's number.

quiz.prompt: True or false: A multicast is the right way to apply damage, because then every machine runs the same subtract.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: A multicast would let the client's math run everywhere.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A multicast is the right way to apply damage, because then every machine runs the same subtract.

quiz.prompt: The owning client wants a muzzle flash now, and the server will confirm the shot later. What can be local?
choices: The flash. The damage still waits for the server.
The health subtract, because the flash proves the hit.
The victim's position, which the shooter may set.
The score, which the shooter may add.
quiz.why: Cosmetics can predict. Rules cannot.
quiz.review_prompt: The owning client wants a muzzle flash now, and the server will confirm the shot later. What can be local?

quiz.prompt: A client RPC is used to tell the shooter to play a hit confirm. Who runs that function?
choices: That one client. Not the server's rules, and not the other players.
The server, despite the name.
Every machine, because RPC means replicated.
The projectile actor on the server only.
quiz.why: Client RPC is one machine's cosmetic.
quiz.review_prompt: A client RPC is used to tell the shooter to play a hit confirm. Who runs that function?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Validation of a server RPC belongs in the server function, not in a comment on the client.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The server is the only place the check is real.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Validation of a server RPC belongs in the server function, not in a comment on the client.

quiz.prompt: Reload is requested from a client. Where does the magazine actually change?
choices: On the authority, after it checks the mag and the reserve.
On the client, inside the RPC call site, before the server runs.
In OnRep, which fills the mag when it notices a button press.
In the widget, which edits the ammo text.
quiz.why: The server reloads. The client asked.
quiz.review_prompt: Reload is requested from a client. Where does the magazine actually change?

quiz.prompt: True or false: If the server RPC is reliable, the client's damage argument becomes trustworthy.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Reliable means it arrives. It does not mean the argument is honest.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: If the server RPC is reliable, the client's damage argument becomes trustworthy.

quiz.prompt: A cheat sets the RPC argument for the equipped item id. What stops a client from equipping a weapon they do not own?
choices: The server checks the request against the real inventory before it writes EquippedId.
Nothing. EquippedId is whatever the client says.
The widget refuses to draw locked guns, which is the only check.
OnRep reverts the mesh but leaves the id.
quiz.why: The server owns the id.
quiz.review_prompt: A cheat sets the RPC argument for the equipped item id. What stops a client from equipping a weapon they do not own?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Calling the server function directly on a client, without an RPC, runs it with authority.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: A direct call on the client is still the client.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Calling the server function directly on a client, without an RPC, runs it with authority.

quiz.prompt: What does the victim see if every client applied the shooter's RPC argument instead of the server's result?
choices: Different health on different machines, and a kill that only some of them agree happened.
One shared health, because clients average their RPCs.
No shots, because multicast blocks weapons.
The server pauses.
quiz.why: One decision, made on the server.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the victim see if every client applied the shooter's RPC argument instead of the server's result?
